answer: Behavioral thread correlation. Each identity's transaction history forms a thread; the system periodically samples a random beacon timestamp and clusters identities whose action timing and counterparty graphs align too tightly after that beacon. Sybil clusters get flagged retroactively. An attacker must maintain divergent behavior per identity for months, paying real coordination and operational cost per account—roughly the cost of running independent, non-overlapping agents—while any ember of correlated activity risks collapsing the whole set.
